title: Props, every state
prompt: Paint one sheet of cut-out puppet parts for a paper-puppet film, using the attached image. Panel A is the exact layout, panel B is our footage for these props (reference: copy the object, not the photo style), panel C is the style. STYLE (panel C): flat cards cut from corrugated cardboard, gouache with confident ink linework, the flutes faintly showing through the paint, a thin raw kraft-brown cut edge round every card, brass split-pin brads; shot flat-on, even light, no shadows, no perspective. Copy the craft from C, not the clothes in it. WHAT (panel B): the props of the poem 'Out of Life', one row each, every state of a prop in its own cell, left to right: the vape pen and its ember: slim black pen, the tip a tiny glowing point that outlives everything else in the film (held, ember breathing, exhaling cloud, falling, still lit, alone on black); the poem: one printed A4 sheet, creased in four, the type visible as grey lines (No still in the index fits; designed from the treatment and the world module.) (read aloud, crumpled, words falling as tumbling dashes); the window and fire escape: a sash window with a cross mullion, and outside it a steel landing and rail (open, EX outside, receding, empty); the dresser drawers: three plain wooden drawers with brass pulls, pulled out and pushed in by nobody (No still in the index fits; designed from the treatment and the world module.) (shut, pulled open, empty); the TV: flat TV on a low stand showing world chaos (No still in the index fits; designed from the treatment and the world module.) (world chaos, flicker); escape screens: floating phone- and TV-shaped panes: pills, parties, feeds (drifting past the fall); the hole in the parquet: a ragged black hole in herringbone parquet (No still in the index fits; designed from the treatment and the world module.) (closed, opening, open black). Paint each state as a flat cardboard prop card at the size its cell gives, the same object across its row; a brass brad on the green cross (its pivot); where there is a red cross, that is where a hand grips it. LAYOUT (panel A): paint one card inside each grey ghost, in the same place, size and angle, inside its dashed outline; a brass brad exactly on every green cross; each red cross must fall inside that card's rounded end. NEVER draw a pelvis, hip, shorts or briefs card (the thighs end in a rounded seat that tucks under the hem), a sleeveless vest, lace-up boots, or sunglasses painted onto a head. OUTPUT: only the painted cards on a pure white 2048x1152 sheet laid out as panel A. Leave out panels B and C, the crosses, labels, ruler, dashed lines and ghosts.
